answer: An agent economy can anchor identity to a secret key sealed inside trusted hardware, like a ship nailed to its keel. A newcomer presents an attestation from a secure enclave that cannot be cloned or resold, and posts a bond bound to that key. A sybil farm cannot split one real identity into a thousand heads, because the chip refuses to sign twice and cannot be rented away. Every fake needs its own device and stake, so cost climbs per identity instead of spreading across a botnet. Honest agents dock once; impostors stack like timber on a wharf, each paying before the harbor lets it through.
